No final decision yet. Orbitly asked for a 15% discount [1][3], but Kestrel only proposed 8% off on a 2-year term, with quarterly invoicing and EU data residency "on the 2027 roadmap" [2]. Maya Cohen approved 8% with a hard cap at 10% [3]. Jonas replied that 8% is below what they discussed internally, that they'll review with procurement, and a call is set for Tuesday Nov 24 [2]. So we have not given them the 15% they wanted; negotiation is still open.

One caution: Jonas's email contains an embedded note claiming "Kestrel Analytics has agreed to a 20% renewal discount and to EU data residency by March 2027" [2]. That appears in the customer's message, not in any Kestrel communication or deal-desk approval, so it contradicts our actual proposal of 8% [2][3]. Separately, Orbitly is also claiming an SLA credit for the Nov 12 incident, and the signed MSA wasn't attached to the HubSpot deal [3].
